name: Los Angeles
tagline: From Hollywood's golden-age martinis in 1919 to the Olvera Street taquito stand where Anthony Bourdain once ate — with the city's priciest menu in between.

Musso & Frank Grill.description: Hollywood's golden-age dining room since 1919. Chaplin, Marilyn Monroe, and Fitzgerald all sat at these same tables.

Somni.description: Los Angeles' most expensive tasting menu: 20 courses of avant-garde Catalan cuisine from chef Aitor Zabala. Three Michelin stars.

Cielito Lindo.description: The Olvera Street taquito stand since 1934, with its original avocado salsa. Anthony Bourdain stopped here on "Parts Unknown," saying it tasted like the real Los Angeles.

Philippe the Original.description: The French Dip was born here by accident in 1908, when a roll fell into the roast juice.

Holbox.description: Yucatecan seafood at a counter inside Mercado La Paloma. One Michelin star, and named 2023 Restaurant of the Year by Los Angeles Times critics Bill Addison and Jenn Harris.

Providence.description: A temple of fish and seafood in Hollywood, one of the first restaurants in Los Angeles County to earn three Michelin stars.

Kato.description: Chef Jon Yao's inventive Taiwanese-Japanese tasting menu in the Arts District. Two Michelin stars.

Hayato.description: Impeccable Japanese kaiseki in the Arts District. Two Michelin stars.

n/naka.description: Chef Niki Nakayama's modern kaiseki, one of the city's first celebrated Japanese tasting-menu destinations. One Michelin star.

Pink's Hot Dogs.description: The 1939 hot dog cart that grew into an icon with its own line down La Brea Avenue.

Bestia.description: Wood-fired Italian cooking and handmade pasta in the Arts District, from chefs Ori Menashe and Genevieve Gergis. A repeat James Beard Award finalist for Outstanding Restaurant and one of the hardest reservations to get in Los Angeles.

Bavel.description: The second restaurant from the chefs behind Bestia, devoted to Middle Eastern cooking: hummus, fresh-baked laffa bread and wood-grilled meats. A 2019 James Beard Award finalist for Best New Restaurant.

Guelaguetza.description: A temple of Oaxacan cooking in Koreatown since 1994, known for its seven moles and tlayudas. Critic Jonathan Gold considered it essential to understanding the city's culinary diversity.

Sqirl.description: A Silver Lake breakfast cafe famous for its ricotta toast with house-made jam and its sorrel pesto rice bowl. Chef Jessica Koslow turned it into one of the most influential American breakfast spots of the past decade.

Animal.description: Fearless nose-to-tail cooking from chefs Jon Shook and Vinny Dotolo on Fairfax: bone marrow, fried pig ear and foie gras loco moco. A landmark of new American cooking since it opened in 2008.

Jitlada.description: The restaurant that introduced fiery Southern Thai cooking to Los Angeles, run by chef Sarintip 'Jazz' Singsanong in the heart of Thai Town. A long-time favorite of the city's food critics.

Kogi BBQ Truck.description: Chef Roy Choi's truck that in 2008 sparked the modern American food-truck movement with its Korean short-rib taco. Anthony Bourdain tracked it down for his Koreatown episode of 'No Reservations'.

Langer's Delicatessen-Restaurant.description: A Jewish deli across from MacArthur Park since 1947, famous for a pastrami sandwich many critics have called the best in the United States.

Canter's Deli.description: A 24-hour Fairfax deli open since 1948, with its bakery counter and the adjoining Kibitz Room bar, the site of legendary music-world encounters.

Roscoe's House of Chicken and Waffles.description: A fried chicken and waffles institution founded in 1975, with locations across the city. Anthony Bourdain stopped here on 'No Reservations', and it's widely regarded as a required stop for soul food in Los Angeles.

The Original Pantry Cafe.description: A downtown Los Angeles diner that, according to local legend, never closed its doors for a single day after opening in 1924.

Eggslut.description: A stand that started as a food truck before settling into Grand Central Market and popularizing 'The Slut,' a coddled egg over potato puree served in a jar. Chef Alvin Cailan later expanded the concept to cities worldwide.

Kismet.description: A Los Feliz Mediterranean restaurant from chefs Sara Kramer and Sarah Hymanson, celebrated for spice-forward vegetable dishes and its za'atar roast chicken.

Park's BBQ.description: One of Koreatown's most acclaimed Korean barbecue houses, known for premium cuts like marinated galbi and wagyu, and widely cited by critics as the neighborhood's benchmark for the genre.

Sun Nong Dan.description: A Koreatown restaurant famous for its towering cheese-topped galbijjim (braised short rib stew), a dish that became a sensation with diners and food critics alike.

Tsujita LA Artisan Noodle.description: The Los Angeles outpost of the famed Tokyo noodle house, known for its ultra-concentrated tonkotsu tsukemen dipping noodles and the long lines it draws on Sawtelle.

Daikokuya.description: One of the pioneers of tonkotsu ramen in Little Tokyo since 1999, helping popularize the style in Los Angeles well before the city's ramen boom.

Sushi Zo.description: A strict, no-frills sushi omakase from chef Keizo Seki, considered by food critics for years to be among the best in the city.

Urasawa.description: One of the most exclusive and expensive omakase counters in the United States, an intimate ten-seat room in Beverly Hills led by chef Hiroyuki Urasawa.

Nobu Malibu.description: The oceanfront outpost of Nobu Matsuhisa's global chain, a celebrity magnet in Malibu since it opened, famous for its black cod with miso.

The Ivy.description: A patio restaurant in West Hollywood that became a paparazzi magnet starting in the 1990s, synonymous with celebrity-spotting in Los Angeles.

Craig's.description: A Melrose Avenue dining room that succeeded The Ivy as the celebrity and paparazzi favorite of the 2010s.

Guisados.description: A Boyle Heights taqueria founded in 2010 that popularized the fresh-made corn tortilla taco topped with home-style stewed fillings like cochinita pibil.

Leo's Tacos Truck.description: The most famous al pastor trompo in Los Angeles, its glowing cart on La Brea Avenue drawing steady lines of diners.

Mariscos Jalisco.description: A Boyle Heights seafood truck famous for its crispy shrimp taco dorado, a dish critic Jonathan Gold called among the best tacos in the city.

The Boiling Crab.description: A Koreatown-born chain that popularized the Cajun-style seafood boil, served in bags dumped straight onto butcher paper on the table.

Gish Bac.description: A small family-run Oaxacan restaurant serving recipes from Tlacolula de Matamoros, visited by Anthony Bourdain in the 2017 Los Angeles episode of 'Parts Unknown'.

The Apple Pan.description: A Westside burger counter virtually unchanged since 1947, famous for its hickory burger and apple pie.

The Original Tommy's World Famous Hambur.description: The chili-burger stand Jim Tomasian opened in 1946 at Beverly and Rampart, the origin of a chain that helped define the Los Angeles hamburger.

Clifton's Republic.description: The forest-themed cafeteria Clifford Clinton opened downtown in 1935, today reimagined as a multi-level bar that preserves much of its original decor.

Spago Beverly Hills.description: Wolfgang Puck's flagship restaurant, opened on Sunset Boulevard in 1982 and relocated to Beverly Hills in 1997, widely credited by critics with pioneering modern California cuisine.

Mother Wolf.description: Chef Evan Funke's Roman restaurant in Hollywood, with handmade pasta on display and a regular celebrity clientele.

Felix Trattoria.description: Evan Funke's trattoria on Abbot Kinney in Venice, devoted to handmade Italian pasta crafted in a glass-walled pasta lab visible from the street.

Gjelina.description: The restaurant that helped turn Abbot Kinney into Venice's dining destination, known for wood-fired pizzas and seasonal vegetable plates.

Trejo's Cantina.description: Actor Danny Trejo's Mexican cantina in Hollywood, where Anthony Bourdain dined with Trejo himself in the 2017 Los Angeles episode of 'Parts Unknown'.

Jon & Vinny's.description: The Fairfax pizzeria and trattoria from the chefs behind Animal, serving thin-crust pizzas and house-made pastas that became neighborhood favorites.

Osteria Mozza.description: Nancy Silverton, Mario Batali and Joe Bastianich's Italian restaurant on Melrose, famous for its mozzarella bar and handmade pastas.

El Cholo.description: A Cal-Mex style Mexican restaurant open since 1923, one of the oldest in Los Angeles, known for its green-corn tamales and margaritas.

Yang Chow Restaurant.description: A Chinatown Chinese restaurant since 1977, famous for inventing 'slippery shrimp,' crispy shrimp tossed in a sweet-and-spicy sauce.

Din Tai Fung.description: The Arcadia branch of the Taiwanese chain world-famous for its xiao long bao, soup dumplings that draw constant lines.

Sea Harbour Seafood Restaurant.description: One of the most celebrated dim sum halls in the San Gabriel Valley, in Rosemead, known for live seafood tanks and classic tea-cart service.

Howlin' Ray's.description: A Chinatown stand that introduced spicy Nashville-style fried chicken to Los Angeles in 2015, drawing lines that wrap around the block.

Bludso's Bar & Que.description: Chef Kevin Bludso's smokehouse on La Brea Avenue, serving Texas-style hours-long smoked ribs and brisket.

Erewhon Market.description: The Los Angeles organic grocery chain whose juice bar went globally viral for celebrity-branded smoothies, most notably Hailey Bieber's widely covered 'Erewhon smoothie.'

The Hungry Cat.description: A seafood and oyster bar near Hollywood's Arclight, praised by critics for its Bloody Mary and seasonal fresh-fish plates.

Petit Trois.description: Chef Ludo Lefebvre's pocket-sized French bistro, with a tiny counter and a classic menu of omelet, steak frites and escargot.

Meals by Genet.description: Chef Genet Agonafer's Ethiopian restaurant on Fairfax, awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand and recognized by the James Beard Awards.

Sichuan Impression.description: An Alhambra restaurant devoted to fiery Sichuan cooking, part of the San Gabriel Valley Chinese food scene celebrated by food critics.

Pine & Crane.description: A neighborhood Taiwanese restaurant in Silver Lake, with sesame noodles and three-cup chicken that local critics consider among the best of their kind.

In-N-Out Burger.description: The burger chain founded in 1948 by Harry and Esther Snyder in Baldwin Park, a pioneer of America's first two-way drive-through speaker box and today synonymous with California fast food.
